scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your power bank says ten thousand milliamp hours, but it doesn't charge your phone even twice. Why not?

scenes.name: cells
scenes.text: A power bank is basically lithium ion cells, the same kind as your phone, plus a small circuit board.

scenes.name: voltage
scenes.text: The cells work at about three point seven volts, but USB needs five volts or more. So a boost converter steps it up.

scenes.name: loss
scenes.text: That conversion loses some energy as heat. And the rating is measured at the lower cell voltage.

scenes.name: real
scenes.text: So a ten thousand milliamp hour bank typically delivers around six to seven thousand to your phone. Not the full number.

scenes.name: protect
scenes.text: The circuit also guards against overcharging, short circuits and overheating, which is why cheap unbranded ones can be risky.

scenes.name: fly
scenes.text: Because of the battery inside, airlines want power banks in your cabin bag, never in checked luggage.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Cells, boost, losses, protection. Energy in your pocket. Follow for more on how things really work.
